title: Start finding commonality between CAN wiretaps
description:
Use socketcan.[c|h] for shared (Socket)CAN functionality where the wiretaps create records of the  WTAP_ENCAP_SOCKETCAN encapsulation type.

Adjust existing "homegrown" structures to use as much of the "shared" data structures from socketcan.h so that all can use the single function wtap_socketcan_gen_packet() to create records.

notes.body: This is not something that is intrinsic to SocketCAN, but depends on the specific file type, and maybe it can vary between files.

You're not wrong, but I am trying to get the wiretaps to behave the same as much as possible. For the two cases you brought up:

1. I'm okay with USEC precision even when the file type only has MSEC precision, I don't think the extra zeros hurt.
2. There is code logic that implies some files may not have a timestamp, but I have yet to see a capture file that doesn't. As seen in the patch, the WTAP_HAS_TS flag can be turned off (in the unlikely event of no timestamp) - However this seems to be more of an "error check" to ensure the header information specified a time format.  Unsure what should be done if one isn't specified and a timestamp is found with a line of data.
